main_text.head: PRÆLECTIO NONA.
De Legum Humanarum Obligatione ex parte Caufæ Finalis.
1 Tim. II. 2.

p.i: —Pro Regibus, & pro omnibus qui in Sublimitate constituti sunt: ut quietam & tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate & honestate.

main_text.p: I.DE Legum Humanarum Obligatione quod ad Caufam Materialem, Efficientem, Formalem attinet, prout res tulerat (fusius alicubi fortassis, alibi contracius, quàm par erat,) egimus utcunque superioribus præleCtionibus: supereft ut ad ea quæ ad Legum caufam Finalem pertinent dubia pertractanda pergamus porrò. Sed antequam ad illa dubia diffolvenda perveniam, illud interim præmittendum est, & ut res indubia fupponendum, Legum ultimum finem effe Bonum communitatis, five pacem & 1.tranquillitatem publicamLe[?]. Probatur hoc primò, ex ipsis iftis Apostoli verbis, [ἵνα ἤρεμον καὶ ἤσυχον βίον διάγωμεν[?], ut vitam quietam & tranquillam agamus.] Hortatur nimirum hic Apostolus,

page.notes: Page is a scan of a printed book with show-through from the reverse side (faint text at top and in the upper right-hand area) and smudges; these are not transcribed. The left-edge strip belongs to the neighbouring page and is excluded. The Greek line in the bracketed quotation is only partly legible; the transcription of it is uncertain. The running head at the top is very faint and may be partly show-through, hence the [?]. The catchword "ac" at the lower right is uncertain. The marginal "1." and "Le" are small and faint; "Le" is especially doubtful. The page is numbered 239 at top right.
